papers.title_en: Memory-Augmented Online Test-Time Adaptation for EEG Motor Imagery via Perturbation Consistency and Confidence Calibration
papers.authors: Kunkun Zhang, Kehao Wu, Zhitao Chen, Haigen Hu, Qianwei Zhou
papers.evidence: 提出用于EEG运动想象的无源在线测试时适应方法以处理跨受试者分布偏移
papers.tldr: 本文针对脑机接口中 EEG 运动想象的非平稳和跨被试分布偏移问题，提出源无关的记忆增强在线测试时自适应框架 MOPC。该框架在推理阶段实时更新解码参数，通过随机掩码扰动一致性、置信度校准重加权损失和轻量记忆模块，实现单次自适应并防止遗忘。在 BCI IV IIb 和 OpenBMI 数据集上分别超越现有方法 2.22% 和 3.67%，自适应延迟约 40-60 ms。
papers.abstract_en: Recently, electroencephalography (EEG)-based brain--computer interfaces (BCIs) have gained traction as portable neural measurement systems. However, the practical deployment of these instruments is often hindered by nonstationarity and cross-subject distribution shifts, which lead to significant intersubject inconsistency. Existing adaptation methods remain impractical for real-time measurement scenarios, as they typically require offline access to source or aggregated target data. To address these challenges, this article proposes memory-augmented online test-time adaptation (OTTA) with perturbation consistency and confidence calibration (MOPC), a source-free framework designed to enhance the reliability of BCI instrumentation. MOPC enables the measurement system to update its decoding parameters on the fly during the inference stage, facilitating single-pass adaptation without accessing sensitive source data. We introduce random-mask perturbations to enforce prediction consistency against inherent EEG signal noise and acquisition artifacts. Furthermore, a confidence-calibrated reweighting loss is designed to integrate feature-space similarity, effectively mitigating unreliable pseudolabels and class imbalance during continuous signal acquisition. To ensure system stability and prevent the catastrophic forgetting of established neural patterns, a lightweight memory module is incorporated to regularize parameter updates within a tight latency budget. Evaluated on the BCI IV IIb and OpenBMI datasets, MOPC achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming prior methods by 2.22~\% and 3.67~\%, respectively, while keeping the per-trial adaptation latency to approximately 40--60 ms. This study provides a robust, recalibration-free solution for real-time EEG decoding, marking a significant advancement in the precision and usability of practical BCI measurement instruments.

papers.title_en: EEG-Captioner: Grounding EEG-to-Language Generation in Fundamental Signal Properties
papers.authors: Leyuan Jin, Jiahao Mei, Yixuan Yuan, Shimeng Li, Mengyue Wu, Yue Ding
papers.evidence: 基于信号属性的EEG到语言生成，用于神经信号解码
papers.tldr: 针对 EEG-to-language 模型难以验证是否真正理解信号的问题，该研究构建了包含 160,781 个带信号级问答对和 captions 的数据集，并提出双域 EEG 编码器与统一框架 EEG-Captioner，同时用信号级 QA 和 caption 监督训练。实验表明，该方法在问答任务上取得 88.81% Macro-BA，并将 caption 事实一致性从 82.06% 提升至 83.46%，验证了两种监督的互补性。
papers.abstract_en: Electroencephalography (EEG)-to-language models offer a promising approach for translating complex neural signals into human-readable descriptions. However, generating plausible language does not necessarily demonstrate that a model has learned to interpret the underlying EEG signal. A direct way to assess such interpretation is to probe objectively measurable properties of the signal itself. We therefore construct an EEG-language dataset of 160,781 segments annotated with signal-level question answering (QA) pairs, where each question targets one of five property families and requires a quantitative comparison involving spectral, spatial, temporal, or lateral signal properties. Each segment is also paired with a feature-grounded EEG caption. We further propose a Dual-Domain EEG Encoder that jointly models temporal waveforms and spectral-spatial representations, and introduce EEG-Captioner, a unified EEG-to-language framework trained with both signal-level QA and EEG caption supervision. Experiments show that the proposed encoder achieves the highest overall macro-averaged balanced accuracy (Macro-BA) among the compared EEG encoders, while EEG-Captioner achieves a Macro-BA of 88.81% on signal-level QA and improves caption factual consistency from 82.06% to 83.46% over caption-only language adaptation, demonstrating the complementary benefits of signal-level QA and caption supervision.

papers.title_en: DRAFT: Decoding and Reconstructing 3D Room Layouts from fMRI and Camera Trajectories
papers.authors: Chi-Wei Lee, An-Kai Chen, Cheng-Han Chiang, Yi-Chun Chang, Po-Chih Kuo
papers.evidence: 仅从fMRI信号重建3D房间布局
papers.tldr: 针对从移动视角恢复房间度量几何的挑战，本文首次提出仅用相机轨迹和fMRI信号重建未见场景3D布局的任务。方法DRAFT从早期视觉皮层提取布局表示，融合相机运动自由空间，在10个场景上layout r达0.480，优于相机路径和七个fMRI解码器，且可作为插件提升所有解码器性能。
papers.abstract_en: While functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) decoders reconstruct images and 3D objects, recovering the metric geometry of rooms from a moving viewpoint remains an open challenge. We introduce, to our knowledge for the first time, the task of reconstructing 3D layouts of held-out scenes using only the known camera trajectories and the fMRI signals of participants watching indoor walkthroughs, without any visual frames. The task is hard because of the temporal mismatch between rapid visual changes and blurred fMRI signals. Our method, DRAFT (Decoding and Reconstructing 3D room lAyouts from fMRI and Trajectories), extracts a compact layout representation from the early visual cortex and fuses this neural code with the geometric free space derived from camera motion. To evaluate it, we propose layout r, the Pearson correlation between predicted and ray-cast log depths. On ten held-out scenes (20 participants), DRAFT reaches a layout r of 0.480, outperforming the camera path alone (0.446) and seven fMRI decoders (at most 0.429). DRAFT also works as a plug-in that improves all seven decoders without retraining, raising their layout r from 0.171-0.429 to 0.487-0.493. Brain activity and camera motion can thus recover the metric layout of unseen rooms, a first step toward reconstructing the 3D spaces people see.

papers.title_en: Spectral Uncertainty Decomposition for Sparse Bayesian Learning
papers.evidence: M/EEG源估计的谱不确定性分解
papers.tldr: 针对M/EEG源成像的不适定逆问题，本文提出基于先验预条件前向算子奇异值结构的谱分解框架，将后验协方差精确分解为数据知情分量与不可约不确定性分量，并推导等价减法分解，区分可被更好测量减少与根本不可减少的不确定性，为线性高斯贝叶斯逆求解器提供可解释的不确定性量化工具。
papers.abstract_en: Estimating distributed neural sources from M/EEG measurements is an ill-posed inverse problem where principled uncertainty quantification remains challenging. The usual conditional Gaussian posterior covariance does not explicitly distinguish uncertainty along likelihood-visible source directions from uncertainty that is invisible to the measurements. We propose a spectral framework based on the singular value structure of the prior-preconditioned forward operator, which provides an exact, interpretable decomposition of the posterior covariance into data-informed and indeterminacy epistemic components. This formulation identifies uncertainty contributions that are reducible by better measurements from those that are fundamentally irreducible by sensing geometry. We further derive an equivalent subtractive decomposition that expresses the prior covariance as the sum of posterior and data-driven reduction terms, enabling precise accounting of uncertainty reduction through Bayesian learning. Together, these complementary representations offer both theoretical insight and practical tools for interpretable uncertainty quantification in M/EEG source imaging for linear-Gaussian Bayesian inverse solvers where the posterior covariance is available in closed form.

papers.title_en: Gate-Based Feature Importance in Simulation-Based Inference for EEG: A Cautionary Tale
papers.authors: Shrivatsa Deshmukh, Sasha Brenner, Thomas R. Knösche, Nico Scherf
papers.evidence: 检验特征门控在脑电仿真推理中的可解释性
papers.tldr: 本文研究仿真推断中特征门控权重的可解释性。作者在脑电图计算神经科学场景下，用神经后验估计推断 Jansen-Rit 模型参数，比较学习门控权重与消融基准的特征重要性。结果显示两者显著负相关，门控降权了消融认为最重要的特征，但预测精度几乎不受影响。研究提示在科学机器学习流程中应谨慎解读门控权重为因果特征重要性。
papers.abstract_en: Simulation-based inference (SBI) provides a powerful way to fit mechanistic models to data, but offers little insight into which information in the data shapes the inferred parameter values. It could therefore benefit from robust and inexpensive interpretability methods. Learned weighting mechanisms such as feature gates provide a potential route to low-cost interpretability, although their interpretation assumes that predictive training reveals which inputs drive performance. We examined this assumption in a computational neuroscience setting, where neural posterior estimation (NPE) is used to infer four physiological parameters of a dynamical model of interacting neuronal populations (Jansen-Rit). We tested whether the learned gate weights captured feature importance by comparing them with a retrain-based ablation benchmark, in which each feature was removed in turn and the NPE retrained. We considered two jointly trained gates: independent sigmoid weights and competing softmax weights. If these reliably reflect feature importance, they should align with the ablation-based estimates. Across nine independent training seeds, however, gate-based and ablation-based importance were negatively correlated (Spearman's rho approximately -0.61 for sigmoid gating and -0.56 for softmax gating). The feature that ablation identified as most important, total signal power, was among the features the gate down-weighted most, despite gating costing negligible predictive accuracy. These results extend a pattern previously documented for attention mechanisms in natural language processing and for explainability methods in electroencephalography (EEG) deep learning to the simulation-based inference setting, and suggest caution when interpreting learned gate weights as measures of causal feature importance in scientific machine-learning pipelines.
